title: Gypsy tart
subtitle: The Kentish tart of whipped evaporated milk and dark muscovado sugar
excerpt: Gypsy tart is a Kentish speciality: evaporated milk and dark muscovado sugar beaten together for a full 15 minutes until the mixture becomes a pale, airy foam, then poured into a blind-baked pastry shell and baked for just 10 minutes. The filling sets to a light, moussey texture that contrasts with the crisp pastry.
sourceNotes: Gypsy tart is strongly associated with Kent, particularly the Sheppey and Thanet areas, and was a common school dinner dessert in the county from the 1930s to the 1980s. The recipe is documented in Kentish food heritage literature. The unusual texture comes from the prolonged whipping of evaporated milk, which incorporates air into an otherwise very simple mixture.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Bake and chill on the day of serving. The filling weeps if stored longer than 24 hours.

baking.bakeTemperatureNote: Conventional oven, 200 degrees Celsius for the blind-baked pastry and for the filled tart. The filling sets in 10 minutes; watch carefully.

glossaryTerms.definition: The unusual setting mechanism of gypsy tart: evaporated milk and muscovado sugar whipped together for 12 to 15 minutes form an airy, pale foam. This foam bakes in 10 to 12 minutes and sets to a light, almost moussey texture. The tart should still wobble in the centre when removed from the oven; it firms completely as it cools.

content.text: only works if the evaporated milk is thoroughly chilled before whipping and the whipping is sustained for a full 12 to 15 minutes. Five minutes is not enough; the foam will not hold in the oven. The tart looks done when the surface is set but the centre still has a distinct wobble; this is correct.

items.prepNote: bought, or use the quiche lorraine pastry recipe
1 large tin, chilled overnight in the fridge

content.text: Roll out the shortcrust pastry and line a 23 cm tart tin. Chill for 30 minutes. Blind bake at 200 degrees Celsius with baking paper and baking beans for 20 minutes, then remove the beans and paper and bake for a further 8 to 10 minutes until the pastry is golden and fully set. Leave in the tin.

Pour the chilled evaporated milk into the bowl of a stand mixer. Add all the dark muscovado sugar. Whisk on the highest speed for 12 to 15 minutes. The mixture will transform from dark brown to a much paler, airy foam. It should have roughly doubled in volume and hold a soft ribbon when the whisk is lifted.

Pour the foam immediately into the blind-baked pastry case. Bake at 200 degrees Celsius for 10 to 12 minutes. The surface should be set and lightly coloured but the centre still wobbles when the tin is gently moved.
Cool completely in the tin, then chill for at least 1 hour before slicing. The filling sets firmer as it cools. Serve cold.

A fully set, wobble-free gypsy tart in the oven will have a granular, slightly gritty texture when cold. The wobble is not under-cooking; it is the aerated foam still setting. Trust the wobble and remove it from the oven on time.
